steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Monokpo-street, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1426 | 2.2 | 2.2
2 | 569 | 0.998 | 3.2
3 | 1241 | 23.2 | 26.4
4 | 1931 | 30.1 | 56.5
5 | 2994 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as Q-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Monokpo-street, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Monokpo-Street, Bori Metropolis**

The VES interpretation at this station reveals a five-layer subsurface sequence. Resistivity decreases from Layer 1 (1426 Ω·m) to Layer 2 (569 Ω·m), then rises progressively through Layers 3 (1241 Ω·m), 4 (1931 Ω·m), and 5 (2994 Ω·m). This pattern reflects an initial high-resistivity layer, a shallow low-resistivity zone (possibly clay or saturated material) between 2.2–3.2 m depth, underlain by increasingly resistive formations extending beyond 56.5 m — consistent with a deepening competent or coarser-grained aquifer unit.

Based on the resistivity trend (r1 > r2 < r3 < r4 < r5), the curve-type sequence derived from the three-layer groupings is **H-A-A**, not Q-type as stated in the file. A true Q-type curve requires continuously decreasing resistivity with depth, which is not observed here due to the resistivity rebound after Layer 2. The on-file classification should be corrected.
